The Hebrew heading ends with a full stop, which the English keeps.
segments.note: Heading of the author's introduction, as the decisions give it.

segments.english: Let the enlightened man reflect, and let the fearful and trembling man lament over the word of the LORD, over the state of the people of Israel, upon seeing that every people and each people, of all the divisions of the nations, cherish their tongue and magnify their language, in which they were educated. Their faith and their religion were engraved in it, each man in his own tongue. And we, the people of Israel, since the time that we were exiled from our land, have abandoned our holy tongue, in which the first Adam spoke and in which our holy Torah was given, when His glory, may He be blessed, was revealed on Mount Sinai, and He said to His people, I am the LORD your God, etc., and we have not done as we were commanded, and you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them. And as Rashi of blessed memory explained in Parashat Ekev, “from here they said: ‘When the child begins to speak, his father speaks with him in the holy tongue and teaches him Torah.’” Thus far his words, but all our conversation with our children is in the language of the people among whom we dwell, and most of the children’s teachers too, are not able to speak all their needs in the holy tongue, even though they know it, for they have not tried these, and there are no systems for teaching the children of the elementary school. It is known and famous, the compassion of the father for his sons, and how many toils and exertions the parents exert in raising their children. With most of their attention on all their children’s needs: his food and his drink, suited to him, his bedding, and his clothing! But when he comes, eager to bring him into school, he casts him off with a teacher of children, in narrow and dark houses, on remnants of mats on the ground, without cleanliness, for the teacher does not clean the children’s abode, only from one foot to the next. All day they sit crowded, without order, and breathe foul and musty air. And they drink salty water, and because of this, when some months pass since he was brought to school, growths and a bad boil come up on his head. And their fathers do not look after them to bring them clear, sweet water to drink, nor clean bedding to sit on, and on most days they sit on the ground without a mat! In the new era, from the year 5650 of the full count of creation, many of the enlightened were stirred and sought an organisation of the schools and an organisation of their children for the study of Torah and the study of the languages Hebrew, Arabic and Turkish, which are in use! And they strove to seat enlightened teachers in the Torah of the LORD, to manage the children of the school in moral upbringing and cleanliness of the place of learning, in bright houses and spacious windows in order to breathe fresh and clean air! And all the labour of those enlightened men came to nothing, and their plan did not come to fruition, and the children of the elementary school remained as they were, with a teacher, in dark and musty rooms, sitting in a crowd: this one learns the alef-bet, and this one learns Scripture, and this one learns with the Targum of Onkelos and the translation of Rabbi Saadia Gaon in Arabic, without understanding. Also the very smallest, who are not at all fit to learn, like a child of two and three years, are brought there. And many times the child relieves himself there. And the teacher sends to his mother that she should come and wipe her son’s excrement! And at the call of the reader of the periodicals in those days, from Mr. Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, for the revival of the holy Hebrew language, our soul yearned only for words and mere conversations, and it did not come to realization until the year 5670, when our exalted government, the government of Turkey, then deigned to open schools for the children of Israel, and there was made there a fine organisation for the children of Israel, in spacious upper rooms with open windows, and bedding of wool, and cloths of goat-hair, and also tables for the older children to learn and to write on them! Then we said: behold, the time has come to bring out Ashtonot Ish Yerushalayim, may it be rebuilt and established, which before she began to bear the great man in the revival of the Hebrew language, namely Eliezer Ben-Yehuda, and we acknowledge our debt to him for what he did and made, and with all his strength he toiled for the good of the people of Israel and the settlement of the land of Israel and the revival of the Hebrew language; this holy work he performed with wondrous alacrity and diligence; he made it succeed and raised it from the dust, and after its decay it had a new bloom, and because of his love for the holy tongue its wrinkles were smoothed out, and the appearance of its face showed itself and blossomed, and it found grace and honour in the eyes of its seekers, its knowers, and its acquaintances, and they awoke from their sleep to gird up their senses, to widen it and to enrich it as in the days of its youth, before the exile of the people of Israel! And because of this mitzvah, may his soul be bound up in the bundle of life with the LORD our God, and from the fruit of his labour may his soul be satisfied in Eden, the garden of God!

tokens.note: Yitpa'el jussive: 'let him reflect', a wish addressed to the reader, not a plain future.
Vav with a jussive, continuing the wish.
The Name as written (ה׳ with a geresh), read 'the LORD'.
Abbreviation of yitbarakh, 'may He be blessed'; placed where the Hebrew places it.
The author's 'etc.' marks a truncated quotation of Exod 20:2; see apparatus.
Closes Rashi's words; the quotation is Rashi's, citing the Sages.
Beit rabban, 'house of the master': the traditional elementary school.
A year without the thousands: 5650 of the era from creation (lefirat gadol).
The word is obscure; 'in a crowd' is by sense.
Aramaic form of the alphabet's first two letters, alef and bet.
Onkelos's Aramaic Targum of the Torah.
Saadia Gaon (882-942), his Arabic translation of Scripture.
Lit. 'letters of the times', the periodicals.
Mr., an honorific abbreviation here, not the Name, though written ה׳.
5670 of the era from creation; the civil year is in apparatus.
Togarmah, the Hebrew name the author uses for Turkey.
Ashtonot, lit. 'reflections' or 'thoughts', the title.

tokens.gloss: may it be rebuilt and established
tokens.note: Tav-vav: may it be rebuilt and established (Jerusalem).
Aramaic idiom, rendered by its sense: a public acknowledgement of debt.
Gan Elohim, the garden of God.

grammar: יתבונן and ויתאונן are jussives (hitpa'el): 'let him reflect' and 'and let him lament', a wish addressed to the enlightened and the fearful, not a plain report.
בראותו is a construct infinitive with a pronominal suffix, 'upon his seeing'; the clause that follows, אשר כל עם ועם ..., states what he sees.
Rashi's quotation runs from כשהתינוק to תורה, introduced by שמכאן אמרו ('from here they said') and closed by עכ״ל. The words before it are the author's own.

ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם is Deut 11:19 in the second person plural, embedded in the first person plural of ולא עשינו: the author speaks for the community, and the verse's 'you' is the people it addresses.
segments.note: This paragraph is in the author's own voice (the publisher's voice begins at 1:10). The Hebrew full stops are kept as the English sentence breaks, and the long periods are divided into sentences without dropping a clause.
apparatus: Deut 11:19, 'ולמדתם אותם את בניכם לדבר בם', embedded without quotation marks (tokens 75-80).
Exod 20:2, 'אנכי ה' אלהיך', the opening of the Decalogue, cited with the author's וכו' ('etc.'), so the English keeps 'etc.'.
1 Sam 25:29, 'צרורה בצרור החיים את ה' אלהיך' ('the bundle of life'), with the author's אלהינו for אלהיך.
Ezek 31:9, 'גן האלהים' ('the garden of God'), compared with the author's 'בעדן גן אלהים'.
The Rashi reference is the author's: 'בפרשת עקב' (Parashat Ekev); no verse is given.
Dates: 5650 is about 1889-1890 and 5670 is about 1909-1910 of the civil calendar; the text gives no civil year.
Wikisource text: no collation with the 1931 scan has been made, so any Wikisource addition is translated as base text (Q2).
context: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda (1858-1922) led the revival of Hebrew as a spoken language, in Jerusalem.
Beit rabban, 'house of the master', was the traditional elementary school; the author says children there learned the alphabet and Scripture with a translation, without understanding it.
